anchor: GS3.1 Indian economy: monetary policy transmission and liquidity management
argumentsAgainst: A short-term VRR operation addresses transient liquidity needs but does not by itself resolve durable or structural liquidity imbalances.
Auction-based allocation may not ensure that every eligible participant receives the full amount sought.
argumentsFor: It enables the RBI to inject short-term liquidity in response to evolving near-term conditions.
Variable-rate bidding allows the auction to discover the borrowing rate rather than automatically supplying funds at a fixed rate.
The one-day tenor and specified reversal date support fine-tuning while limiting the operation’s duration.
background: The Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF) includes repo operations for liquidity injection and reverse-repo operations for liquidity absorption.[2]
A VRR auction allows eligible participants to bid for central-bank liquidity at variable rates; the RBI then conducts the operation within the notified amount and tenor.
The source record refers to operational guidelines issued in the RBI press release dated January 20, 2022, but does not reproduce those guidelines.
indiaImplications: The operation can help moderate temporary money-market tightness and support orderly transmission of monetary-policy signals.
Short-term liquidity support may reduce pressure on overnight funding conditions, while the next-day reversal limits prolonged monetary accommodation.
The RBI’s calibrated use of VRR illustrates the distinction between fine-tuning liquidity and changing the policy stance; the source does not state that the policy rate or stance changed.

mainsPractice.stem: Examine how an overnight Variable Rate Repo auction under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility can address near-term liquidity conditions while preserving policy flexibility.

officialFacts.text: The notified amount for the Variable Rate Repo auction was ₹50,000 crore.
The tenor of the Variable Rate Repo auction was one day.
The auction window was 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM.
The date of reversal was October 23, 2026 (Friday).
The RBI decided to conduct a Variable Rate Repo auction on Thursday, October 22, 2026, after reviewing current and evolving liquidity conditions in the near term.
The operational guidelines for the auction were to be the same as those given in the RBI’s Press Release 2021-2022/1572 dated January 20, 2022.

example.heading: Hypothetical illustration
example.text: If banks faced a temporary shortage of funds, an overnight VRR auction could provide liquidity for one day, with the funds reversed on the following working day. This would address a short-lived mismatch without implying a permanent change in the policy stance.

pocketRead.excerpt: The RBI scheduled a ₹50,000 crore, one-day VRR auction for October 22, 2026, with bidding from 09:30 AM to 10:00 AM and reversal on October 23.

question.answer: The operation injects liquidity temporarily through the LAF, while variable-rate bidding enables market-based allocation and the next-day reversal limits the duration of support. It should therefore be read as fine-tuning, not automatically as a policy-rate change.
question.prompt: How can an overnight VRR auction support liquidity management without necessarily signalling a change in the RBI’s monetary-policy stance?

sections.heading: RBI’s announced operation
paragraphs: The RBI announced the auction after reviewing near-term liquidity conditions. It notified ₹50,000 crore for a one-day operation on October 22, 2026, with a 09:30 AM–10:00 AM window and reversal on October 23, 2026.

The operation is conducted under the LAF, where repo operations inject liquidity and reverse-repo operations absorb it.[2] A variable-rate auction uses bids rather than an automatically fixed auction rate.

sections.heading: What the operation can and cannot show
paragraphs: Temporary liquidity injection can ease short-lived funding mismatches and help orderly money-market functioning. The defined tenor and reversal date make the intervention reversible.

The announcement does not state that the RBI changed its policy rate or monetary-policy stance. Nor does it provide the underlying size or cause of the liquidity mismatch; those should not be inferred from the notice.

use: Use VRR to explain how the RBI fine-tunes short-term system liquidity through an auction-based, reversible operation under the LAF. Pair it with the distinction between liquidity management and a change in the monetary-policy stance.

advisory_notes: The LAF definition is useful background, but the supplied notice itself does not define LAF or establish its full set of instruments.
The claim that variable-rate bidding enables rate discovery is sound background, but it is not stated in the supplied notice and should remain explanatory rather than source-attributed.
The claim that VRR allocation may not give every participant the full amount sought is a general auction implication, not a fact established by this notice.
“Support orderly transmission” is a reasonable analytical implication, but the notice does not report any transmission effect or money-market outcome.
The phrase “next-day reversal” is potentially unclear because the notice specifies reversal on October 23 after the October 22 auction; retain the explicit dates.
The distinction between VRR and VRRR is relevant, but the supplied notice concerns only VRR and does not itself establish the full comparative framework.
The hypothetical shortage example is appropriately labelled, but it should not imply that banks actually faced such a shortage because the notice gives no diagnosis.

The proposed GS3.1/GS3.2 anchor is substantively relevant; however, the official UPSC syllabus wording is broader than these internal codes, so label them as study codes rather than official syllabus codes.

wayForward: Use VRR and related operations in a calibrated manner based on observed liquidity conditions rather than treating every liquidity fluctuation as a policy shift.
Communicate the operation’s amount, tenor, auction window and reversal clearly to improve market predictability.
Assess whether liquidity pressure is transient or durable before relying on short-term operations; the source notice itself does not provide that diagnosis.
